requirement_text.REQ-001a: GitHub issue #2 ("Translate to UZ" / "Add localization") requires Uzbek localization of the AI Qadam landing site. This requirement is the first of two: it proves the i18n MECHANISM end-to-end (dependency, routing, middleware, a working switcher) using only src/app/layout.tsx's strings as the seed catalog. REQ-001b (depends_on this requirement) extracts the remaining 12 landing components' copy once the mechanism is proven working. Translation quality is out of scope for both (that is REQ-002). Chosen approach: adopt next-intl as the i18n library. The switcher reuses the .nav/.nav-in/.lang classes already defined in src/app/globals.css (lines 36-51) -- this project's own bespoke CSS variable set, not the documented design-system tokens; stays on globals.css as-is. Scope: add next-intl dependency; restructure routing so src/app/page.tsx and src/app/layout.tsx move under src/app/[locale]/ with locale resolution proxy/middleware, ru default + uz second locale; create messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json seeded ONLY from src/app/layout.tsx's current strings (title, description, OG title/description/locale, Twitter title/description), uz values placeholder-duplicated from ru; replace Nav.tsx's non-functional RU/UZ/EN switcher with a working ru/uz-only switcher (drop EN) using next-intl's locale-aware routing helpers and only the existing .lang/.lang span/.lang .on classes; src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx sets <html lang> dynamically and localizes metadata title/description/OG locale (ru_RU/uz_UZ) from the message catalog; root / redirects to /ru.

task.description: Implement REQ-001a exactly per docs/agents/design/REQ-001a.md (do not freelance structure it didn't specify — if it's wrong or incomplete, report rather than silently improvising). CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASSed the design with one legitimate open question left for you to resolve here: Next.js 16 deprecated middleware.ts in favor of proxy.ts (confirmed against Next's own docs) — once you add next-intl as an actual dependency, check ITS OWN docs/exports (node_modules/next-intl or its README/types) for which convention it expects on Next 16, and use whichever is actually correct for the installed version — don't guess, verify against the installed package. Follow WF-02 Step 2's procedure: verify you're on branch feature/WF02-REQ-001a before touching any file (STOP and report FAIL if not), implement per the design, run npm run lint (fix and retry on FAIL), run npm run build (fix and retry on FAIL), then self-review against frontend_developer_guide.md §4's checklist including checking both light/dark theme and mobile/desktop width for the switcher specifically.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation matches docs/agents/design/REQ-001a.md's structure (file tree, message catalog keys, switcher props/behavior) -- any deliberate deviation is reported, not silent
No raw hex colors introduced; only var(--token-name) and the cited existing .lang/.nav classes reused
Visiting /uz renders <html lang="uz">, visiting /ru or / renders <html lang="ru">

Nav.tsx switcher has exactly two working options (RU, UZ), navigates correctly between /ru/* and /uz/* preserving section anchors, checked in both light and dark theme and at a mobile and desktop width
messages/ru.json and messages/uz.json exist with matching key sets, uz values placeholder-duplicated from ru
